patch_description: The current algorithm routes each destination independently with Dijkstra, and then replicates the exact same path for every partition. This causes massive redundant transfers: if two destinations share a path prefix, the data is sent over the same links multiple times, and each partition duplicates the whole route. A much cheaper broadcast structure is a Steiner tree: data is forwarded once over shared links and only splits where destinations diverge. I use the classic shortest-path-heuristic Steiner tree approximation (iteratively connect the nearest unconnected destination to the current tree), which yields a single low-cost multicast tree. Then I assign partitions to the tree edges, and to balance load across networks, partitions after the first are routed via alternative low-cost paths (k-shortest simple paths) when available, spreading traffic across parallel network links while keeping costs low. This reduces both redundant transfers (shared tree edges) and per-partition duplication cost, directly minimizing total data transfer cost.
